items.title: POF
items.text: In Your love, hear us Oh Lord

items.lyrics:
Protocol Overhead: Network packets include framing, headers, and control data (TCP/IP overhead) that consume about 5% to 6% of the raw line rate, leaving a maximum theoretical payload capacity of roughly 940 to 950 Mbps.

Hardware Bottlenecks: Real-world speeds also depend on your computer's network interface card (NIC), the CPU load, and the speed of your storage drives when transferring local files.

Cabling Issues: Using older cables like Cat5 instead of Cat5e, Cat6, or higher can force your connection speed to drop down to the 100 Mbps tier
